title: Machine-learning validation and independent cross-checks classify 50 Kepler candidates as planets
summary: A Gaussian-process classifier, supported by random-forest, extra-trees and multilayer-perceptron models, was applied to Kepler transit candidates. From 83 candidates meeting the study’s stringent ML and data-quality criteria, the authors newly validated 50 as planets after updated vespa false-positive checks also gave each less than a 1% false-positive probability. The result is statistical validation using Kepler pipeline and stellar data, not new telescope observations of the planets.
ai_technology: Gaussian process classifier, random forest, extra trees and multilayer perceptron classifiers

evidence.tested: A Gaussian-process classifier, supported by random-forest, extra-trees and multilayer-perceptron models, was applied to Kepler transit candidates.
evidence.unknown: The 50 are statistically validated candidates from archival Kepler observations, not newly observed planets. The authors caution that their method is trained and demonstrated on Kepler, that atypical/outlier candidates may be unreliable, and that ML and vespa disagree for 33 other high-ML candidates; those were not counted as validated. This entry counts one paper-level validation result, not 50 separate records.
evidence.ai_role: Four machine-learning classifiers jointly ranked candidate transit signals against planet and false-positive scenarios. The paper required all four to cross 0.99 planet probability plus positional, stellar, binary and outlier checks; an updated vespa calculation then independently cross-checked the retained candidates.
